summary: Smart Alert Triage (/alerts) backend + frontend verified end-to-end. 24/25 backend tests PASS (1 skipped — admin had no HOLD alert); all key frontend flows work with zero console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: AlertsPage.jsx onTake() uses `alert?.id && window.alert(msg)` where `alert` parameter shadows window.alert — `alert.id` is truthy here so `window.alert(msg)` fires fine, but the shadowing is fragile; rename the param or use `window.alert(msg)` directly.

routers/alerts.py _resolve_pending: hardcoded limit of 50 per call could leave alerts perpetually unresolved if a user has >50 pending across multiple stats calls that fail partway — acceptable but worth a TODO or pagination.
AlertsPage load() swallows errors silently in the finally — a failed /alerts/stats call leaves stats=null forever without user feedback.
Payload dicts on star/archive/taken accept missing keys silently (bool(None) -> False). Pydantic model would catch bogus payloads earlier.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing admin alerts; cleaned up star/taken state after each test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_alerts_triage.py is the regression suite for this feature. Every action test (star/archive/taken) resets state in a finally block so the suite is re-runnable. The taken-lifecycle test makes a REAL yfinance call on AAPL (or MSFT/TSLA/any BUY/SELL fallback). HOLD rejection test is skipped for admin since admin currently has no HOLD-signal alerts — ok. Frontend verified via Playwright: /alerts route, 4 KPI cards, 5 filter tabs, 18 alert cards, star toggle, ticker deeplink to /analysis/{ticker}?autorun=1, empty state on taken filter, mobile drawer nav-alerts link, zero console errors. `Took it` UI click was not exercised (covered by backend lifecycle test + real yfinance call from UI would leave state to clean). /api/alerts endpoints at router prefix /alerts under api_router /api — final path /api/alerts/*.
